entities.summary: Flavius Strategius Apion was a patrician and jurist of the Eastern Roman Empire, serving as the sole Roman consul of 539 CE. A member of the wealthy Apion family of Oxyrhynchus, Egypt, he played a significant role in the administrative and legal systems of the Eastern Roman Empire. Apion's legacy extended to the preservation of Roman law and governance in the Eastern provinces, shaping the administrative structures of the Byzantine Empire. His contributions to the codification of Roman law had a lasting impact on the development of legal systems in the Mediterranean world. Strategius Apion's life and works are a testament to the enduring influence of the Eastern Roman Empire on the trajectory of human civilization. The Byzantine Empire's continued reliance on Roman legal traditions reflects the lasting legacy of Strategius Apion's work.
